next.name: GOLD LOCUST
next.headline: GOLD LOCUST: the financially driven group also tracked as FIN7 and Carbanak
next.in_short: GOLD LOCUST is the catalogue name for a group also called FIN7 and Carbanak. Vendors describe a financially motivated actor that hit hospitality and retail, then moved toward ransomware and tools that disable security software.

sentences.t: The catalogue record lists Anunak, Carbanak, Carbon Spider and FIN7 as other names for GOLD LOCUST.
The catalogue names Carbanak as the actor's tool.
SentinelOne describes FIN7 as an elusive, persistent and financially motivated threat group with origins in Russia.
SentinelOne says that beginning in 2020 the group shifted its focus to ransomware, affiliating with ransomware-as-a-service groups such as REvil and Conti.
FireEye said in 2017 that FIN7 kept causing havoc in the restaurant, hospitality and financial services sectors.
SentinelOne lists hospitality, energy, finance, high-tech and retail as industries that suffered losses. It also names US manufacturing, legal and public sector companies.
In 2020 the FBI warned that FIN7 was mailing packages through USPS to retail, restaurant and hotel businesses.

The Hacker News reports that Carbanak, a banking malware detected in the wild since at least 2014, has been used by FIN7. NCC Group saw it used in ransomware attacks, with installers posing as business software such as HubSpot, Veeam and Xero.
In the FBI's account, the mailed USB drives were set up to act like a keyboard and type commands. The aim was to deliver the GRIFFON malware.
Morphisec describes a FIN7 chain that started with a phishing lure and ran script stages in memory. It ended with a script that loaded Carbanak by reflective loading.
FireEye reported that in April 2017 FIN7 shifted to running JavaScript through wscript.exe. It also described FIN7 hiding shortcut files in phishing documents.

SentinelOne assesses with high confidence that several forum sellers of tools that disable antivirus belong to the FIN7 cluster. The tool it tracks is AvNeutralizer, also called AuKill, and SentinelOne says it uses a newly seen driver-based method to tamper with security products.

SentinelOne says FIN7 adopted automated SQL injection attacks. It attributes these intrusions to the group with medium confidence. It cites Prodaft's earlier finding that the group built the Checkmarks platform for this.
Harfanglab says the developers of the PackXOR packer, used with AvNeutralizer, might be connected to the FIN7 cluster. It adds that the packer appears to be used for activity unrelated to FIN7.
BleepingComputer reports that in 2018 the FIN7 syndicate hacked Saks Fifth Avenue and Lord & Taylor to steal payment card information.
Malwarebytes attributed a malspam campaign in late June 2022 to FIN7. It dropped JSSLoader, a rewrite of the loader with data exfiltration, and a second .NET payload.
S2W reports that Darkside, known to be used by the FIN7 group, was rebranded as BlackMatter.
SentinelLABS tied custom EDR evasion tools used in Black Basta ransomware attacks to FIN7 in a report published on 3 November 2022.
In its July 2024 report, SentinelOne cannot conclusively say whether LockBit intrusions involving AvNeutralizer were carried out by FIN7. It says no direct evidence links them to the group.
Treat unexpected mailed USB drives and invoice-themed attachments as hostile, and protect security tools against tampering.
